_note: Hand-written market take, refreshed twice a day (~8am and ~8pm UTC) by a separate scheduled research pass. Not touched by scripts/sync.py's automatic hourly sync. This is the site's hero paragraph (first thing under the H1 title). Not financial advice.
text: Bitcoin ripped from around $76,000 to a high near $81,500 in just two days, and even after a slight pullback to about $80,300 this morning it's still up sharply from where it sat last week. The move came right after the Fed's quarter-point hike to 3.75-4.00% barely rattled markets, and stocks holding up gave crypto holders room to stay patient through the wobble. What really flipped the picture was Friday's Bitcoin ETF buying spree -- a single-day inflow of $433 million, led by Fidelity and BlackRock, that rescued the week from a second straight net outflow and dragged sentiment out of caution and into outright greed, with the Fear and Greed Index jumping from 56 to 71 in a day. Trading volume nearly doubled alongside the rally, which is the kind of real-demand confirmation that was missing during the shakier, leverage-heavy action a few days ago. Ethereum funds told the opposite story, breaking a four-week inflow streak and bleeding $140 million for the week, suggesting money is rotating back toward Bitcoin rather than flowing into crypto broadly. The morning dip after such a fast run isn't unusual and doesn't undo the shift -- it looks more like normal digestion of a big move than the start of a reversal. Taken together this looks like a market that just found its footing again, and as long as ETF buyers keep showing up on dips, the path of least resistance for now leans up rather than down.
